episodes.title: What is Organic Chemistry?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’re talking about the amazing diversity among organic molecules.

episodes.title: The Basics of Organic Nomenclature
episodes.description: We'll dive into IUPAC systematic naming of organic molecules, and get to practice with the help of three trusty steps!

episodes.title: More Organic Nomenclature: Heteroatom Functional Groups
episodes.description: Learn IUPAC naming rules for additional functional groups, including groups containing oxygen.

episodes.title: 3D Structure and Bonding
episodes.description: Use hybridization and valence bond theory to understand molecular shapes, constitutional isomers, and geometric isomers.

episodes.title: IR Spectroscopy and Mass Spectrometry
episodes.description: On this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’re learning about mass spectrometry and infrared spectroscopy through the lens of a forensic investigation.

episodes.title: Alkanes
episodes.description: Explore alkanes, Newman projections, molecular strain, common conformers, and cycloalkanes.

episodes.title: Cyclohexanes
episodes.description: Examine cyclohexane ring strain, boat and chair conformations, and how ring flips change substituent positions.

episodes.title: Stereochemistry
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry we’re learning about stereochemistry and how to identify molecules as chiral or achiral.

episodes.title: More Stereochemical Relationships
episodes.description: Review stereoisomer relationships, polarimetry, and predicting how many stereoisomers a molecule can have.

episodes.title: Polarity, Resonance, and Electron Pushing
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’re learning about electronegativity, polarity, resonance structures, and resonance hybrids.

episodes.title: Acidity
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’ll learn four key factors that we can use to predict relative acidity.

episodes.title: Nucleophiles and Electrophiles
episodes.description: Identify nucleophiles and electrophiles and explore nucleophilic attack, infrared evidence of reactions, and cyanide chemistry.

episodes.title: Intro to Reaction Mechanisms
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’ll learn all about how to write reaction mechanisms.

episodes.title: E/Z Alkenes, Electrophilic Addition, & Carbocations
episodes.description: Review alkene naming, carbocations, and Markovnikov’s rule for predicting addition-reaction products.

episodes.title: Thermodynamics and Energy Diagrams
episodes.description: Use thermodynamics, kinetics, energy diagrams, intermediates, transition states, and catalysts to understand organic reactions.

episodes.title: Alkene Addition Reactions
episodes.description: Break alkene addition mechanisms into simpler steps and use guiding questions to recognize reaction patterns.

episodes.title: Alkene Redox Reactions
episodes.description: Track carbon–oxygen bonds to understand alkene oxidation and reduction and predict reaction products.

episodes.title: Alkyne Reactions & Tautomerization
episodes.description: Explore alkynes and compare their reactions with the reactions of alkenes.

episodes.title: Radical Reactions & Hammond’s Postulate
episodes.description: Examine radicals, the stages of radical reactions, Hammond’s postulate, and radical reactions with hydrocarbons.

episodes.title: Intro to Substitution Reactions
episodes.description: Compare SN1 and SN2 substitution mechanisms, substrate preferences, and an application in chemotherapy.

episodes.title: Substitution Reactions – SN1 and SN2 Mechanisms
episodes.description: Compare the SN1 and SN2 pathways for organic substitution reactions.

episodes.title: E1 and E2 Reactions
episodes.description: Explore elimination reactions, E1 and E2 mechanisms, Zaitsev’s rule, and their relationship to substitution reactions.

episodes.title: Determining SN1, SN2, E1, and E2 Reactions
episodes.description: Use substrates, nucleophiles, and reaction conditions to predict which substitution or elimination mechanism will occur.

episodes.title: Alcohols, Ethers, and Epoxides
episodes.description: We’ll use alcohols as a starting point to get other types of compounds like ethers, epoxides, and more!

episodes.title: Synthesis and Column Chromatography
episodes.description: We’re heading into the lab to learn about one of the ways we can separate chemicals in a mixture: chromatography!

episodes.title: How to Identify Molecules – Proton NMR
episodes.description: Learn how proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectra reveal molecular structure and help identify organic compounds.

episodes.title: An Overview of Aldehydes and Ketones
episodes.description: Review aldehydes and ketones and explore their roles in familiar substances, hormones, and medical treatments.

episodes.title: Organometallic Reagents and Carbanions
episodes.description: We’ll learn all about organometallic compounds, including what they are and what kind of reactions we see them in.

episodes.title: Aldehyde and Ketone Reactions – Hydrates, Acetals, & Imines
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, Deboki Chakravarti will teach you about the addition reactions of oxygen and nitrogen-based nucleophiles.

episodes.title: Carboxylic Acids
episodes.description: Review carboxylic acid naming and synthesis, then form salts, esters, and acid chlorides.

episodes.title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives & Hydrolysis Reactions
episodes.description: Compare carboxylic acid derivatives, their reactions with nucleophiles, and hydrolysis mechanisms used in penicillin synthesis.

episodes.title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives – Interconversion & Organometallics
episodes.description: Explore carboxylic acid derivatives, their relative reactivity, reduction reactions, and their role in synthesizing penicillin.

episodes.title: Chemoselectivity and Protecting Groups
episodes.description: In this episode, we’ll look at what makes a good protecting group, as well as identify some good protecting groups for different functional groups.

episodes.title: Retrosynthesis and Liquid-Liquid Extraction
episodes.description: Practice retrosynthesis and multistep organic synthesis, and learn about liquid–liquid extraction as a laboratory separation technique.

episodes.title: Polymer Chemistry
episodes.description: We’ll look at different examples of addition and condensation polymers, learn about different types of polymerization, and see how a polymer’s morphology affects its properties.

episodes.title: Aromaticity, Hückel’s Rule, and Chemical Equivalence in NMR
episodes.description: We’ll learn all about aromatic compounds, their properties, reactivities, and some of the most important examples, like benzene.

episodes.title: Intro to Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
episodes.description: Use electrophilic aromatic substitution to attach halogens, carbon groups, and other substituents to benzene rings.

episodes.title: More EAS - Electron Donating and Withdrawing Groups
episodes.description: Learn how electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituents influence further aromatic substitution reactions.

episodes.title: More EAS & Benzylic Reactions
episodes.description: Explore limitations of Friedel–Crafts reactions, substitution with multiple directing groups, and reactions at benzylic positions.

episodes.title: Synthesis, Distillation, & Recrystallization
episodes.description: Learn distillation and recrystallization, then apply laboratory techniques to aromatic substitution and synthesis problems.

episodes.title: Conjugation & UV-Vis Spectroscopy
episodes.description: Explore conjugation, molecular stability, pi molecular orbitals, and what ultraviolet spectroscopy reveals about conjugated molecules.

episodes.title: The Diels-Alder & Other Pericyclic Reactions
episodes.description: Explore pericyclic reactions, including DNA damage from ultraviolet light and the Diels–Alder reaction.

episodes.title: Enols and Enolates - Reactivity, Halogenation, and Alkylation
episodes.description: We’ll learn all about enols and enolates, their reactivity, and reactions we can do with them including halogenation and alkylation.

episodes.title: The Aldol and Claisen Reactions
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’ll learn what an aldol is, as well as how aldol reactions work and what they do.

episodes.title: Crossed Aldol Reactions, Enones, and Conjugate Addition
episodes.description: We’ll learn about crossed aldol reactions, the formation of kinetic and thermodynamic enolates, hard and soft nucleophiles, conjugate addition, and of course, enones!

episodes.title: Amines
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Organic Chemistry, we’ll explore amine formation and basicity, and revisit some old friends, imines and enamines!

episodes.title: Diazonium Salts & Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution
episodes.description: Explore how nitrous acid produces diazonium salts and learn the conditions needed for nucleophilic aromatic substitution.

episodes.title: Biochemical Building Blocks & Fischer and Haworth Projections
episodes.description: Explore biochemical building blocks and convert carbohydrate structures between Fischer and Haworth projections.

episodes.title: Biological Polymers
episodes.description: Examine the building blocks of biological polymers, including carbohydrates, proteins, and DNA.

episodes.title: Medicinal Chemistry and Penicillin Total Synthesis
episodes.description: Explore medicinal chemistry through penicillin’s action, protein synthesis, and the completed synthesis of penicillin V.
